title: Apprentice Insights 6mo Pilot Plan
body:
Purpose and context:
This is a six-month pilot to evaluate an Apprentice program targeted at early-career engineers and career-changers with strong aptitude but atypical CVs. The objective is twofold: (1) create an inclusive, low-friction pipeline that reliably converts high-potential apprentices into full-time contributors; (2) experiment with a compact interview + onboarding rubric and an accelerated 60-day activation path that reduces ramp time for ICs in product-facing teams.

Why now:
- Hiring velocity in Q2–Q3 has shown candidate dropoff early in the funnel for junior roles.
- Engineering teams report high onboarding variability for junior hires; mentorship capacity exists this fiscal year for experiments.
- Strategic priority to diversify entry points while improving time-to-impact metrics.

Pilot scope and capacity:
- Cohort size: up to 8 apprentices total across two cohorts (4 per cohort).
- Duration: 6 months (two 8-week cohorts with a 4-week evaluation and potential conversion window).
- Roles: front-end, infra-tooling, and ML-infra shadow slots prioritized.
- Budget: $160k program budget (stipends, training, tooling credits, mentor time allocation).

Success metrics (primary):
- Conversion rate to full-time: target >= 50% per cohort.
- Time-to-first-PR (developer-facing): median <= 21 days.
- 90-day retention post-conversion: >= 85%.
- Hiring funnel efficiency: applicant->offer conversion improved by 15% for target roles.

Secondary metrics:
- Mentor NPS (survey) >= 4.0/5.
- Candidate experience sentiment >= 4.2/5.
- Cost-per-hire compared to junior hire benchmark.

Candidate profile and sourcing notes:
- Target: career changers with demonstrable project work (bootcamps, OSS, hobby projects), recent grads without formal internships, and internal transfer candidates.
- Must-haves: basic programming proficiency, ability to communicate tradeoffs, strong learning orientation.
- Nice-to-haves: prior team collaboration on multi-file projects, basic testing habits.
- Sourcing channels: partner bootcamps, university outreach, internal referrals, alumni networks.

Screening funnel (compact):
1) Application + short project link (1–2 artifacts).
2) 30–45 minute live screen with a recruiting engineer focusing on problem-solving and learning stories. (Pass threshold: demonstrates deliberate practice and one clear learning example.)
3) Compact take-home exercise (3–6 hours) that mirrors an onboarding task (small bugfix + mini-feature).
4) Onsite/virtual loop (2–3 interviews) with rubric scoring and behavioral probe.

Interview rubric (scoring guide, 1–4 scale where 4=strong, 1=insufficient):
- Problem decomposition (scale): Can break a task into reasonable steps; identifies edge cases and tradeoffs.
- Code clarity and correctness: Produces readable, maintainable solutions; tests where appropriate.
- Learning agility: Evidence of rapid learning, accepts feedback, demonstrates iteration.
- Collaboration & communication: Explains thinking, asks clarifying questions, pairs well.
- Product sense & impact orientation: Understands user needs and prioritizes accordingly.
- Ownership & reliability: Shows examples of delivering on commitments; follows through.

Decision rules:
- Each interview returns a numeric score and a binary recommend/no-recommend.
- Minimum pass: average rubric score >= 2.5 and no score of 1 in ownership or collaboration.
- Calibration: All interviewers to attend a 30-minute calibration session before cohort hires start; recording examples of 1–4 for consistent scoring.

Hiring plan timeline (high-level):
- Week -6 to -4: Partner outreach, cohort role definitions, mentor pairing.
- Week -3: Job posting, intake, recruiting kickoff.
- Week -2 to 0: Screens and take-homes. Offer window opens at Week 0.
- Cohort Week 1–8: Onboarding program (see onboarding checklist).
- Week 9–12: Evaluation window (mentor assessments, test projects).
- Week 12–16: Conversion decisions and potential FT offers; feedback retrospective.

Onboarding checklist (cohort-first 8 weeks, high cadence):
Pre-onboard (Week 0):
- Welcome packet and cohort calendar sent.
- Hardware and cloud access provisioned; basic infra templates ready.
- Pairing matrix created (mentor, buddy, rotation schedule).

Week 1 (orientation + small wins):
- Day 0: Welcome sync with People Ops + Eng manager; expectations and milestones.
- Day 1–3: Setup dev environment; run a guided repo-to-PR exercise. Goal: first PR merged.
- End of week: 1:1 with mentor to set learning objectives.

Weeks 2–4 (product immersion):
- Rotational pairing across 2 small micro-projects.
- Weekly learning sessions (code walkthroughs, testing basics, internal system maps).
- Checkpoint: deliver a documented small fix or feature and demo to cohort.

Weeks 5–8 (autonomy and impact):
- Ownership of a slightly larger feature or cross-team bug triage.
- Mentor shadowing decreases; apprentice leads a demo to product stakeholders.
- Bi-weekly feedback loops; checklist for reliability and code quality.

Evaluation rubric for conversion (mentor + manager):
- Impact: Delivered measurable contribution aligned to product goal (S/M/L).
- Technical growth: Demonstrably learned new concepts and applied them.
- Team fit: Communicates and collaborates effectively in cross-functional settings.
- Reliability: Meets commitments and shows trajectory toward independent delivery.

Conversion decision matrix:
- Convert: >=3 of 4 categories rated 3 or higher and mentor recommendation positive.
- Extend trial: mixed signals, still promising but needs more time (paired 1:1 plan).
- No-convert: clear gaps in core outcomes; provide off-boarding resources and closure notes.

Mentorship model and load:
- Ratio: 1 mentor to 2 apprentices (mentors are senior ICs with 0.2 FTE allocated).
- Buddy: peer-level buddy for day-to-day questions.
- Training: mentor enablement doc + 90-minute kickstart session describing learning objectives and feedback cadence.

Risk register & mitigations:
- Risk: Mentor bandwidth insufficient. Mitigation: appoint backup mentors at cohort start; cap cohort size.
- Risk: Low conversion (=costly). Mitigation: use staged offers, small stipends, and tight evaluation windows.
- Risk: Reputational (low candidate experience). Mitigation: candidate comms playbook, survey at 3 touchpoints.

Operational checklist (people ops):
- Stipends and payroll set up before Day 0.
- Access inventory and escalations documented.
- Legal/benefits check for apprenticeship stipend classification.
- Reporting dashboard: invite Managers + People Ops to a weekly cohort update.

Communications plan:
- Pre-apply: public landing page (FAQs, expectations, sample tasks).
- During cohort: weekly public-ish digest with wins and learnings (internal).
- Post-cohort: retrospective and candidate feedback summary; update hiring playbook.

Open questions for review:
- Optimal stipend amount relative to cost-per-hire benchmark? Proposal: $6k per apprentice for 8-week cohort.
- Which teams are best early partners (ML-infra and developer-experience proposed)?
- Conversion offer cadence and compensation banding — align with comp.

Next steps for approval:
- People Ops to finalize budget and legal sign-off (due 2025-10-09).
- Recruiting to confirm sourcing partners and post job (due 2025-10-16).
- Eng leads to confirm mentors and team slots (due 2025-10-16).

Appendix: sample compact take-home exercise outline (attached in Confluence):
- 3-hour exercise: fix a small bug in a toy service + add one unit test + short PR description. Scored for clarity, tests, correctness, and simplicity.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally experimental and lightweight: goal is to learn signals and iterate quickly. Please annotate sections with red/green flags in the Confluence linked artifact.
summary: Pilot plan for a 6-month Apprentice program: cohort design, rubric for interviews, compact onboarding checklist (8 weeks), evaluation and conversion rules, metrics, and operational steps.
